newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds recover losses after strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds recover losses after strong U.S. data.

text.p: Irish government bonds recouped earlier losses in gentle trade on Friday after robust U.S. data surprised European markets, dealers said.
"Trade has been pretty muted and markets are gradually recouping knee-jerk losses suffered after the stronger-than-expected durable goods data in the U.S.," one dealer said.
By 1444 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was 12p stronger at 106.62 to yield 6.00 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 20p at 107.65 to yield 6.78 percent.
U.S. durable goods data rose 4.6 percent in September.
The eight percent bond due 2015 was 110.00, a gain of 25p.
"I think the Dublin market is in snooze-mode ahead of the bank holiday weekend in Ireland now, but we've seen some squaring up of portfolios" one dealer said.
In the UK, gilt prices also slipped after the U.S. durable goods data showed the largest monthly gain since December 1992, but the UK market consolidated towards the close, dealers said.
"Next week there's quite a lot of inflationary data in the U.S. and we also have some money supply figures in the UK," one dealer said.
"We'll certainly have a lot more data to go on than this week," he added.
